title.value: SARS-CoV-2 infection in Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis of standardised seroprevalence studies, from January 2020 to December 2021
title.justification: The title directly states that the paper is focused on analyzing seroprevalence studies of SARS-CoV-2 in Africa over a specified period of time.
title.quote: SARS-­CoV-­2 infection in Africa: a systematic review and meta-­analysis of standardised seroprevalence studies, from January 2020 to December 2021...

extractions.description: This paper is a systematic review and meta-analysis of population-based seroprevalence studies to estimate the exposure to SARS-CoV-2 in Africa, aiming to inform public health and social measures (PHSM) and vaccine strategies. It analyzes seroprevalence differences by demographic groups, place, and time, highlighting the extent of undetected infections.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: While the paper deals with public health data related to COVID-19 in Africa, it does not explicitly focus on Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development, making it peripheral to these themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Estimating COVID-­19 cumulative incidence in Africa remains problematic due to challenges in contact tracing, routine surveillance systems and laboratory testing capacities and strategies...

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily deals with epidemiological data related to a health crisis (COVID-19) rather than climate change or sustainable development topics.
primary_category.quote: We report high seroprevalence in Africa suggesting greater population exposure to SARS-­CoV-­2 and potential protection against COVID-­19 severe disease than indicated by surveillance data.

secondary_categories.justification: No secondary Sustainable Development themes related to climate or ecological impacts are evident in the paper.
secondary_categories.quote: High, heterogeneous seroprevalence in Africa highlights the need for targeted serosurveillance, public health and social measures and vaccination strategies tailored to the local context...
